problem:
Title: Complex Roots of Unity are Vertices of Regular Polygon Inscribed in Circle

Let $n \in \Z$ be an [[Definition:Integer|integer]] such that $n \ge 3$.

Let $z \in \C$ be a [[Definition:Complex Number|complex number]] such that $z^n = 1$.

Let $U_n = \set {e^{2 i k \pi / n}: k \in \N_n}$ be the [[Definition:Complex Roots of Unity|set of $n$th roots of unity]].

Let $U_n$ be plotted on the [[Definition:Complex Plane|complex plane]].

Then the elements of $U_n$ are located at the [[Definition:Vertex of Polygon|vertices]] of a [[Definition:Regular Polygon|regular $n$-sided polygon]] $P$, such that:
:$(1):\quad$ $P$ is [[Definition:Circle Circumscribed around Polygon|circumscribed]] by a [[Definition:Unit Circle|unit circle]] whose [[Definition:Center of Circle|center]] is at $\tuple {0, 0}$
:$(2):\quad$ one of those [[Definition:Vertex of Polygon|vertices]] is at $\tuple {1, 0}$.
